Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image render its visual content as a pencil drawing overall?
node.criteria: Pass if the image as a whole is recognizably rendered in a pencil-drawing style, with pencil-like marks shaping the depicted content; some retained photographic detail or residual color does not by itself prevent a pass. Fail if it remains predominantly photographic or otherwise does not read overall as a pencil drawing, even if it is desaturated or has isolated sketch-like texture. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the overall style cannot be determined.
node.binding: Judge the overall rendering against the requested pencil-drawing outcome while checking that the visual content remains represented. Do not require complete removal of photographic detail or color, and do not treat isolated texture alone as sufficient.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image retains the depicted meal and table setting, while the overall scene has muted, grainy pencil-like shading and drawn contours. It reads as a pencil drawing despite some residual color and photographic detail.

fulfillment: The node’s completion rule is too permissive: it treats s1’s broad “reads overall as a pencil drawing” judgment as sufficient for yes, even though its own evidence notes residual color and photographic detail. The edited image does show substantial pencil-like texture and muted tones, but the reference is partial, so distinguish visible progress from complete fulfillment rather than letting a single positive style impression settle completion. Inspect the binding and criteria for an explicit, evidence-based completion threshold and ensure the partial-progress path can be evaluated when completion is not established. Also repair the dependency/activation structure: the node declares s2 as a parent/dependency in the supplied trace context, but the variable requires only s1, and s2 is conditionally skipped and invalid. Align required dependencies and routing with the intended completion-versus-progress decision so skipped evidence is not mistaken for evidence either way. Treat the invalid skipped s2 as a transport/execution gap, not negative visual evidence; do not infer absence of the requested edit from it. The high-confidence s1 judgment is a signal to review its criterion calibration, not a reason to override the image or force a label.
